q7: Is the condition label the right BUCKET for this finding? The field is a coarse enum, not a precise diagnosis, and `condition` means (population): `condition` names the patient POPULATION the paper studied. A collagen-biology paper with no EDS/HSD cohort is `general` even if it informs EDS; a paper that carries an EDS/HSD label without studying that population is a bucket violation, recorded in the additive annotations table and never corrected in place. Bucket definitions (eds dry-run v1 (2026-09-30); EDS_hypermobility inherited from CONDITION_BUCKET_DEFINITIONS.md v1 and split): hEDS = Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome as the studied population: cohorts diagnosed under the 2017 hEDS criteria, and pre-2017 cohorts the paper labels "EDS hypermobility type" / "EDS type III". Includes hEDS comorbid with POTS, MCAS or GI dysmotility when hEDS is the specific subject. Nearest exclusions: hypermobility spectrum disorder goes to `HSD`; a cohort pooling hEDS and HSD without separate reporting goes to `multiple`; "joint hypermobility syndrome" cohorts without an EDS label go to `hypermobility_unspecified`.; HSD = Hypermobility spectrum disorder (generalized, historical, localized or peripheral HSD, 2017 framework) as the studied population. Nearest exclusions: hEDS goes to `hEDS`; a pooled "hEDS/HSD" cohort goes to `multiple`; Beighton-assessed hypermobility without an HSD diagnosis goes to `hypermobility_unspecified`.; EDS_other_type = Any 2017-classification EDS type OTHER than hypermobile, as the studied population, with the type named in `eds_type`: classical (cEDS), classical-like (clEDS), cardiac-valvular (cvEDS), vascular (vEDS), arthrochalasia (aEDS), dermatosparaxis (dEDS), kyphoscoliotic (kEDS), brittle cornea syndrome (BCS), spondylodysplastic (spEDS), musculocontractural (mcEDS), myopathic (mEDS), periodontal (pEDS), or a newer molecularly defined type.
